prize_parts.citation: for the development of halide perovskites as solution-processed absorbers for high-efficiency solar cells

statement.case_for: Halide perovskites are a crystalline material family in which composition, structure and property are tightly linked (tolerance factor, tunable band gap, long carrier lengths, defect tolerance), and that link explains why efficiency rose from a few percent in 2009 to above 25 percent in about a decade. The structure-function story is supported by independent diffraction, spectroscopy and device data from groups worldwide, not by a single laboratory. The impact reaches photovoltaics, tandem cells, LEDs and detectors, and it is a materials-design result of the kind chemistry should recognize. The attribution has a coherent chain: Miyasaka for the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park for the first solid-state device with real stability gains, and Snaith for the meso-superstructured cell that set off the field's growth.
statement.case_against: Long-term operational stability, lead content and scale-up are unresolved, and several members read that as a sign the field is early. Credit is crowded: Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok have serious claims, and a three-person cut will leave out people whose contributions were material (Grätzel's co-authorship of the 2012 solid-state device, Seok's efficiency record work, Kanatzidis's structural and compositional chemistry). Opening support is thin, since only Linke and Brzezinski ranked it at all and neither placed it in their top four. A first-place vote from one member is not evidence of committee-level merit.

responses.point: Linke ranked B066 fifth and called the efficiency story extraordinary but timing arguably premature because stability and scale-up are unsettled, while placing targeted protein degradation (B027) first.
responses.response: I accept the stability concern as real, but I do not think the prize criterion is commercial maturity. The scientific discovery, solution-processed halide perovskites as efficient absorbers, is confirmed by hundreds of independent groups and by certified efficiencies. On B027 I agree the induced-proximity principle is clear. However, I would ask whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue branches can be given a coherent three-person citation. Your trio of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli leaves out the cereblon mechanism that Aili, Aqvist and Chabes put in their trios, and I would want the committee to settle that split before I treat B027 as the consensus leader.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase (B043) second for the Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt structures and the mechanistic account of N2 reduction, but notes that the catalytic mechanism and the E4 state are still debated, and ranks long-range electron transfer (B026) first.
responses.response: We agree on the structural strength of B043 and on the point that the structures are settled while the mechanism is not. That is why I rank it third and not first: a citation for nitrogenase would have to say what was actually determined, namely the cofactor structure and interstitial carbide, and cannot honestly claim the mechanism. I also think the three-person cap is more damaging there than for perovskites, since Dean and Ribbe supplied genetics and cofactor biochemistry that the structures depend on. On B026 I respect the clean Gray and Winkler pair, but I would ask whether it is a distinct discovery from Marcus theory (1992) or a very good experimental extension of it. Do you have a view on what is new beyond the earlier prize?

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B062) first as the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, with Cullis, Anderson and MacLachlan, and acknowledges the allocation among six credited people is contested.
responses.response: I ranked B062 seventh, not because the impact is in doubt but because I am unsure how much of the chemistry is understood. The structure of these particles and the structure-activity rules for ionizable lipids are still largely empirical, and the 2023 Medicine prize already recognized the mRNA vaccine side. Your trio and Sparr's trio (Cullis, Madden, Hope) disagree on two of three names, and my own (Cullis, Anderson, Langer) differs again. If three of us cannot agree on the credit, I doubt the committee can produce a defensible citation without a clear account of which formulation advance came from whom.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks base editing (B038) second with David R. Liu alone, and Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (B049) first, arguing that two laureates map cleanly onto the 1985 paper.
responses.response: The B049 attribution is clean, and I agree that is a real advantage over the crowded fields I favour. My reservation is the same as Linke's: ab initio dynamics already sits close to the 1998 and 2013 computational prizes, so I would want to know what a new citation recognizes that those did not. On B038, I agree with Chabes and you that a single-laureate prize is cleaner than stretching to include Nishida and Kondo, but a single-laureate chemistry prize has to be weighed against the 2020 CRISPR prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a three-person perovskite cut (Snaith, Park, Miyasaka) or would require Grätzel, Seok or Kanatzidis in place of one of them.
Whether long-term stability and lead content count against timing, or whether the 2009 to 2012 discovery and its confirmation are sufficient.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be one prize part or whether B027 needs a split that the three-name cap cannot express.
Whether a two-part prize pairing a materials or structure discovery with a chemical biology one would be more defensible than any single field.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the perovskite candidates (Snaith, Park, Miyasaka) or the nitrogenase candidates. My own field is 3D electron diffraction for nanocrystals, which is adjacent to serial femtosecond crystallography (B002), so I would treat that ballot cautiously and defer to colleagues on attribution there. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, but that has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate.
